summary: Central Jersey Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics (CJPD&O) is a two-doctor, single-location, privately owned (non-DSO) practice in East Brunswick, NJ, combining pediatric dentistry (Dr. Michelle Backhaus) and orthodontics (Dr. Christopher Overcash) for infants through teens plus special-needs patients. Front-office work is manual and phone/insurance heavy: the practice is hiring a full-time front desk/insurance coordinator (30-35 hrs/week) to handle claims, appeals, scheduling, payments and a busy phone line. Scheduling is a web request form rather than real-time online booking, and after-hours emergencies route to an answering service.

facts.fact: Two doctors, one location, privately owned (non-DSO) practice with many long-term team members, per its own job posting.

Dr. Michelle M. Backhaus is a Board Certified Pediatric Dentist (NYU pediatric certificate 2005) and currently President of the New Jersey Academy of Pediatric Dentistry; Dr. Christopher R. Overcash is the orthodontist (Columbia ortho certificate 2005) and past president of the NJ Association of Orthodontists.
Office address is 176 Summerhill Rd., East Brunswick, NJ 08816, phone (732) 257-5588, per the site's own schema markup.
Hours: Mon/Tue/Thu 8:30 AM-5:30 PM, Wed 10:00 AM-6:30 PM, Fri 8:30 AM-5:00 PM, Sat 8:30 AM-1:00 PM with alternating Mon and Sat coverage.

Services include preventive pediatric care, digital x-rays, nitrous oxide, oral sedation, in-office IV or hospital general anesthesia at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital, soft-tissue laser frenectomy, metal/ceramic/self-ligating braces and Invisalign.
Practice treats infants, children, teens and patients with special needs and draws from East Brunswick, Old Bridge, Sayreville, Monroe and Spotswood.
New patients are asked to request appointments via a web form; the contact page directs people to call or e-mail during office hours only.
After-hours emergencies (for patients of record) go through phone prompts to an answering service, with instructions to call back if no doctor/staff call arrives within one hour.
Named team beyond the two doctors: a Scheduling Coordinator, a Registered Dental Assistant and two Registered Dental Hygienists.

Open role: full-time Front Desk Receptionist/Insurance Coordinator, 30-35 hours/week, alternating Saturdays, with duties covering insurance claim submission and appeals, greeting patients, making appointments, collecting payments and answering busy phones; 2+ years dental experience required and orthodontic treatment coordinator experience a plus.
Benefits listed for the front-desk role: 401(k) plus match, profit sharing, paid time off, sick time and a uniform allowance.
Homepage embeds Google reviews via a Trustindex widget; the ten reviews displayed are all five-star and dated June through November 2025.

operations_signals: Appointment intake is form-based (request, not confirmed booking) with a phone/e-mail fallback during business hours; no real-time online scheduling widget or patient portal is visible on the site (https://kiddent.com/appointment-request/).

Contact page and both web forms carry SMS/text consent language, so text messaging to patients is in use, but messaging appears one-way/broadcast rather than a chat channel (https://kiddent.com/contact-us/).
After-hours coverage is a telephone answering service reached through phone-menu prompts, with a stated one-hour callback expectation (https://kiddent.com/contact-us/).

Staffing model is a scheduling coordinator plus a shared front desk that also handles insurance claims and payments; the practice is actively adding front-desk capacity (https://kiddent.com/about-us/, https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).
Service area is broad for a single location (East Brunswick plus Old Bridge, Sayreville, Monroe, Spotswood), which means new-patient calls come from several townships (https://kiddent.com/about-us/).
Evening coverage exists only on Wednesday (to 6:30 PM) and Saturday hours end at 1:00 PM, concentrating demand into weekday mornings and a single late day (https://kiddent.com/appointment-request/).
hiring_signals: Actively hiring a full-time Front Desk Receptionist/Insurance Coordinator at 30-35 hours/week - a role explicitly built around insurance claim submission and appeals, appointment making, payment collection and busy phones (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).

Posting requires a minimum of two years dental front-office experience and calls orthodontic treatment coordinator experience a plus, indicating the role absorbs both insurance/billing and ortho case coordination (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).

Posting advertises alternating Saturdays 8:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m. and Wednesday evenings until 6:30, i.e., the front desk is expected to cover split/uneven shifts (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).

Retention messaging is explicit - 'many long-term team members that are like an extended family' - alongside 401(k) match, profit sharing, PTO and sick time, suggesting a small, stable staff with one vacancy rather than high churn (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).

No clinical (hygienist/assistant/dentist) openings were found; the only visible vacancy is administrative (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).
review_themes: Consistently positive tone in the reviews the practice surfaces: parents praise a kid-friendly office, patient staff and doctors who explain treatment to children (https://kiddent.com/).
Short wait times are called out specifically, alongside a clean office (https://kiddent.com/).

Front-office accommodation is a recurring compliment - families describe staff as easy to work with and welcoming, and several mention driving long distances to stay with the practice (https://kiddent.com/).
Hygienist/assistant quality for anxious or first-time young patients (including a child with a prior bad experience) is a repeated theme (https://kiddent.com/).
Loyalty and repeat visits over multiple years show up in multiple reviews; the visible sample is uniformly five-star and dated June-November 2025 (https://kiddent.com/).
tech_footprint: Website built on WordPress with Elementor/Elementor Pro and Rank Math SEO PRO, plus a full-screen premium menu plugin - a maintained, agency-style build rather than a template (https://kiddent.com/).
Google Analytics 4 (Site Kit) and Google Tag Manager (GTM-WVDHT4D8) are installed; Site Kit by Google plugin is active (https://kiddent.com/).
Online reputation is managed through a Trustindex Google-reviews widget that auto-syncs Google reviews to the homepage and about page (https://kiddent.com/).
Google Maps embed on-site for directions; Facebook (facebook.com/kiddent) and Pinterest (pinterest.com/kiddentjersey) profiles linked in the footer (https://kiddent.com/).
Accessibility layer present (Equalize Digital/pojo accessibility widget plus skip-link handling) (https://kiddent.com/).
No online booking engine, patient portal, live chat or patient-intake platform detected in the page markup; intake runs on generic forms plus phone (https://kiddent.com/appointment-request/).
Practice contact e-mail published in site schema is a free consumer mailbox (hotmail.com) rather than a domain address, a small-practice operational signal (https://kiddent.com/).

Content footprint is moderate: service pages, five town-targeted pages (Old Bridge, Spotswood, etc.) and an extensive dental FAQ, but no blog with dated articles (https://kiddent.com/dental-services/).
growth_signals: Invisalign was added as a service line (dedicated page updated 2023-2024) alongside existing braces, expanding the ortho offering under the same roof (https://kiddent.com/orthodontics/, https://kiddent.com/invisalign/).

Local-SEO expansion into neighboring towns with dedicated pages for Spotswood and Old Bridge (sitemap last-modified 2024), i.e., actively pushing for new patients outside East Brunswick (https://kiddent.com/page-sitemap.xml).
Steady flow of new Google reviews through November 2025 indicates an active, growing patient base rather than a declining one (https://kiddent.com/).

Owner visibility in organized dentistry: Dr. Backhaus serves as President of the New Jersey Academy of Pediatric Dentistry and is an attending at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital; Dr. Overcash is a past president of the NJ Association of Orthodontists (https://kiddent.com/about-us/).
Awards/badges displayed include 'Favorite Kid's Docs' and Jersey Choice (2018 badge), reflecting past recognition but not recent press (https://kiddent.com/about-us/).

Adding front-desk headcount at 30-35 hours/week is a capacity signal consistent with rising appointment and insurance workload (https://www.wayup.com/i-j-Dental-Front-Desk-Receptionist-Central-Jersey-Pediatric-Dentistry-Orthodontics-006887046316004/).
decision_maker: Dr. Michelle M. Backhaus, Pediatric Dentist and co-owner (practice principal on the site's About page), source: https://kiddent.com/about-us/ ; co-owner Dr. Christopher R. Overcash, Orthodontist, same page

inferences.inference: The front desk is the practice's main operational bottleneck and the most likely entry point for AI agents.
inferences.reasoning: The only open role bundles phone answering, scheduling, payment collection, insurance claim submission AND appeals; scheduling is a request form with no real-time booking; and after-hours calls depend on an answering service with a one-hour callback promise. Those are exactly the tasks an intake/phone/claims-status agent absorbs.

inferences.inference: Insurance administration (claims plus appeals) is a recurring, rules-heavy workload worth automating before clinical workflows.
inferences.reasoning: The job posting names claim submission and appeals as 'necessary skills' rather than incidental duties, which usually means volume and rework. Pediatric practices also carry heavy Medicaid/NJ FamilyCare eligibility churn, though the practice does not publish its payer mix - so payer specifics remain unverified.

inferences.inference: Decision-making is concentrated in two owner-dentists, so a sale is short but must be framed around relieving staff load rather than enterprise integration.
inferences.reasoning: The practice self-describes as two doctors, one location, non-DSO, and both doctors are the named principals on the site. There is no corporate parent, IT department or CTO visible.

inferences.inference: The published Saturday hours (8:30-1:00) understate what the job posting asks staff to cover (8:00-2:00), so real front-desk coverage may be longer than the website implies.
inferences.reasoning: Two primary sources from the same business disagree; the posting is more recent operational evidence than the evergreen hours block repeated in the site footer.

inferences.inference: The visible review sample is curated, so the absence of complaints should not be read as the absence of complaints.
inferences.reasoning: The site displays only five-star Google reviews through a Trustindex slider, and the practice's own reviews page is a solicitation page. Independent rating counts and any negative reviews could not be retrieved during this run.

inferences.inference: Marketing and back-office tooling look good on the front end but thin in the middle office.
inferences.reasoning: GA4/GTM, SEO plugin, accessibility widget and a review-sync widget are all present (front-end polish), while booking, patient intake, chat and a domain e-mail address are absent (middle-office gaps). This pattern fits a small practice that bought marketing services but still runs operations on phone and paper/forms.

inferences.inference: Estimated size is roughly 8-12 people total (2 doctors, 2 hygienists, 1-2 assistants, 1-2 front office), which is consistent with a single-suite pediatric/ortho office.
inferences.reasoning: Derived from four named non-doctor staff on the About page plus a 30-35 hr/week front-desk hire and unusual Saturday/evening coverage. No headcount is published, so this is an estimate only.

data_gaps: Google Business Profile rating and total review count could not be retrieved - web_search providers were rate-limited/unavailable this run and review aggregators (Yelp, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Brave/Bing/DuckDuckGo) returned 403 or captcha pages.
No independent (non-site) review source was opened, so all review themes come from the practice's own Trustindex Google-review widget; negative-review themes are unknown.

Hiring history beyond the single WayUp posting is unverified - no Indeed/LinkedIn/ZipRecruiter listing could be opened to confirm how long the front-desk role has been open or whether other roles were recently filled.
Founding year / years in business not published on the site; doctors' graduation dates (2003-2005) are the only timeline anchors.
Exact staff headcount, number of operatories, patient volume and payer mix (insurance vs Medicaid vs self-pay) are not public.
No pricing, insurance plan list, financing options or membership plan published on the site.
No local news coverage, press releases or expansion announcements found; growth signals are limited to site changes and review recency.

The site's schema markup lists two different ZIP codes (08876 in the Place node, 08816 in the LocalBusiness node) for 176 Summerhill Rd.; 08816 is used here as the East Brunswick ZIP, but the discrepancy is unresolved.
